arguments.value: Progressive dyspnea following COVID-19 infection with bilateral subpleural and bronchovascular CT opacities was initially treated as connective tissue disease-associated interstitial lung disease, but re-review of lung biopsy and BALF testing identified pulmonary Tropheryma whipplei infection superimposed on long COVID. Improved after ceftriaxone, trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole, and steroid taper.
